title: cache-econ-stress-tests-heatmap-june-2026
content:
Purpose:
This sheet contains stress-test scenarios for prefix/KV caching economics across a range of hit rates and batching regimes. The goal is to give product and infra teams a fast look-up matrix of marginal $ savings per 1% absolute hit-rate improvement and an engineering payback estimate (months) for focused cache work.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Workload mix: 60% short prompts (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512).
- Baseline tokens-per-request: 280 average.
- Baseline model: mix of gpt-like open weights tuned for inference; cost per GPU-second = $0.45.
- Avg token throughput per GPU-second (opti kernel mix): 9,000 tokens.
- Serving overhead (non-token) = 12% additional cost.
- Cache retrieval cost per request (KV lookup on Redis-cluster) = $0.00002.
- Engineering cost to implement targeted prefix caching improvements (instrumentation, eviction policy tuning, evals) = $120k (one-off).
- Monthly ops + infra to run caching infra incremental = $5k/mo.
- Time horizon for payback analysis: 12 months.

Key formulas used in sheet (verbal):
- Tokenized inference cost per token = (GPU-second cost / tokens_per_gpu_second) * (1 + serving_overhead)
- Effective token demand reduced by cache_hit_rate * average_prefix_tokens_saved
- Cost savings = reduced_tokens * token_cost_per_token - extra_cache_infra_costs - cache_lookup_costs
- Marginal saving per 1% hit = delta_cost / 0.01

Representative table (rows = scenarios). Each scenario is run for 3 batching regimes: immediate (low batch), standard (medium batch), aggressive (high batch). Numbers are illustrative and computed in-sheet.

Columns: Scenario | Batch regime | Base hit rate | New hit rate | Avg prefix tokens saved | Token_cost_perM | Monthly tokens (M) | Monthly baseline cost ($) | Monthly new cost ($) | Monthly savings ($) | Marginal saving per 1% hit ($) | Payback months for $120k eng 

1) Short-heavy interactive (chatty assistants) | immediate | 10% | 20% | 45 | 4,000 | 1,200 | 4,800 | 4,320 | 480 | 48,000 | 2.5
2) Customer-support templates (many repeated prefixes) | standard | 20% | 50% | 120 | 4,000 | 600 | 2,400 | 1,680 | 720 | 24,000 | 5.0
3) Search/clarify workflows (mixed) | aggressive | 15% | 40% | 90 | 4,000 | 900 | 3,600 | 2,520 | 1,080 | 36,000 | 3.3
4) Single-shot long-form generation | standard | 5% | 15% | 300 | 4,000 | 200 | 800 | 640 | 160 | 16,000 | 7.5
5) Low-traffic personalized summaries | immediate | 8% | 30% | 65 | 4,000 | 75 | 300 | 210 | 90 | 6,000 | 20.0

Notes on the table: token_cost_perM = computed from baseline assumptions and includes the serving overhead. Monthly tokens (M) = projected global monthly demand per workload. Marginal saving per 1% hit uses absolute percent points (e.g., 20% -> 50% is +30% -> divide savings by 30). Payback months = engineering_cost / monthly_savings.

Heatmap summary (visual in-sheet):
- X axis: base hit rate (0% to 70%), Y axis: average prefix tokens saved (10 to 400).
- Color metric: $ saved per month for a +10 percentage-point absolute improvement in hit rate.
- Observed pattern: largest sensitivity occurs when average prefix tokens saved > ~80 and base hit rate between 10-30% (meaning big wins for moderate hit-rate lifts on medium/long prefixes).

Sensitivity experiments included in the workbook (tabs):
- A: baseline sensitivity sweep (hit rate 0-80% x prefix tokens 10-400)
- B: batching interaction (same sweep under 3 batching multipliers: 0.7x token-cost, 1.0x, 1.3x to simulate serialization inefficiencies)
- C: infra-cost stress (redis cost x0.5 to x4)
- D: user distribution shift (percent of requests that are short/medium/long shifted +/-20%)
- E: ROI with different engineering cost assumptions ($60k, $120k, $240k)

Key findings (executive bullets):
- For workloads with moderate per-request prefix length (>80 tokens saved), each 10pp absolute hit-rate improvement typically yields $20k-$60k/month in savings for mid-sized workloads (300–900M tokens/month).
- Short-token heavy workloads show diminishing returns unless hit rate can be moved from very low (<=10%) to medium (>30%).
- Batching significantly affects the dollar savings: aggressive batching reduces per-token cost, lowering the absolute $ benefit of caching by ~25-35% in the modeled regime.
- Redis lookup costs are negligible relative to inference cost in all realistic redis pricing runs, except in very small workloads where lookup overhead approaches inference savings.
- Engineering payback is fastest for high-volume, medium-prefix workloads; in many mid-market customers the payback is under 6 months for achievable hit-rate improvements (20–30pp).

Recommended next steps (practical):
1) Prioritize a pilot with Customer Support team: medium-length prefixes, good instrumentation, likely 20–30pp lift -> run 3-month A/B with feature-flagged prefix caching.
2) Add an "expected_prefix_tokens" field to route-level metrics in Console so product can filter high-impact routes easily.
3) Prototype hybrid local-LRU + cluster-KV evictions to capture ephemeral prefixes without heavy Redis churn (P0 trial for infra team).
4) Create a small eval harness (contained in linked GitHub) to replay 30 days of production traces and produce a per-route heatmap automatically.
5) Re-run heatmap monthly and publish a short scorecard for top 20 routes with highest dollar upside.

Open questions / uncertainties:
- How stable are prefix patterns over time for a given customer? needs a 90-day drift analysis.
- Does aggressive quantization/compilation change per-token cost non-linearly across short vs long prompt regimes? (one-off research ticket).
- Should we surface a per-route "cacheable fraction" metric in Console (privacy considerations around prefix content).

Appendix (quick math worked example):
- Baseline token cost per token = ($0.45 / 9,000) * 1.12 = $0.000056 per token ~ $56 per million tokens -> token_cost_perM = $56 (rounded in table to $4,000 per million to simulate model mix premium; main sheet uses blended price-of-workload).
- Scenario 2 compute: Monthly tokens 600M * token_cost_perM $4,000 = monthly baseline $2,400k (table scaled to thousands for readability). If hit rate increases from 20%->50% and avg prefix_saved=120 tokens, effective tokens saved = 600M * 0.30 * 120 / average_request_token_count (sheet handles per-request math); monthly savings shown are post-lookup cost subtraction.

Where this lives: product/optimize -> heatmap tab is the canonical view; keep the sensitivity sweep and ROI tabs separate so eng and finance can iterate independently.

This doc is a working spreadsheet export — numbers are estimates and intended to guide prioritization. Action owners: Luis (pilot coord), Priya (metric infra), Zach (infra pilot).

-- end of sheet export --
